S57.01.needs: a signed-in account; whether a search runs depends on the model and account
S57.01.note: The search step wording is sent by the server; the extension has no fixed label for the search itself.
steps: Open the side panel and send a question that needs current web information, such as today's news on a topic.
When the answer appears, click the "Worked for …" line under it to open the steps.
Look for a "Sources for …" step and check that it names the search query.
Click the "… sources" button and compare the list under "Sources used for this answer" with Expected.
S57.01.where: Chat > send a question that needs current web information > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > look for "Sources for …" and the "… sources" button

S57.02.note: The fetch step wording comes from the server, so the exact text is not fixed in the extension.
steps: Send a message that gives a full web page address and asks the assistant to read it and summarise it.
When the answer appears, click the "Worked for …" line under it.
Find the step about that page and click it to open the details.
Compare the step with Expected: the fetch should appear with the page it read.
S57.02.where: Chat > ask it to read a specific web page by its link > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > look at the step for that page

S57.03.note: Searched apps/extension for source or document reader labels and found none. Only the server reads PDF and Office files by URL; no extension control was found. The "Add a web page by link" menu item is a different feature.

S57.04.note: Searched apps/extension for file search labels and found none. The file search runs on the server with no extension control found.

S57.05.note: The sandbox file-read tool runs only when AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, which defaults to 0. No extension control for it was found.

S57.06.note: The sandbox file-write tool runs only when AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, which defaults to 0. No extension control for it was found; file outputs show as artifacts (see S57.07).

S57.07.needs: a signed-in account; file creation depends on the account and server
S57.07.note: Some artifacts can show "Download unavailable in Chrome for this artifact." instead of the link.
steps: Send a request such as "Make an Excel spreadsheet of these five items with prices."
When the answer appears, click the "Worked for …" line under it.
Look for the step "Created …" and click its "Open or download …" link.
Check that the .xlsx file opens or downloads, and compare with Expected.
S57.07.where: Chat > ask for an Excel spreadsheet > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > click "Open or download …"

S57.08.needs: a signed-in account; file creation depends on the account and server
S57.08.note: Some artifacts can show "Download unavailable in Chrome for this artifact." instead of the link.
steps: Send a request such as "Write a one-page Word document about this plan."
When the answer appears, click the "Worked for …" line under it.
Look for the step "Created …" and click its "Open or download …" link.
Check that the .docx file opens or downloads, and compare with Expected.
S57.08.where: Chat > ask for a Word document > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > click "Open or download …"

S57.09.needs: a signed-in account; file creation depends on the account and server
S57.09.note: Some artifacts can show "Download unavailable in Chrome for this artifact." instead of the link.
steps: Send a request such as "Make a five-slide presentation about this plan."
When the answer appears, click the "Worked for …" line under it.
Look for the step "Created …" and click its "Open or download …" link.
Check that the .pptx file opens or downloads, and compare with Expected.
S57.09.where: Chat > ask for a slide presentation > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > click "Open or download …"

S57.10.needs: a model and account that can run code; check the model picker's "Code execution" filter
S57.10.note: Availability depends on the model route and the free-trial or managed path; not verified.
steps: Send a message such as "Run this Python code and show the output: print(2 + 2)".
Wait for the "Running code…" line to change.
Open the "Code execution" block under the answer.
Compare the "Output" text with the result the code should print, as Expected says.
S57.10.where: Chat > ask it to run a short piece of code and print a result > under the answer, look for the "Code execution" block and open it

S57.12.note: The sandbox edit tool runs only when AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, which defaults to 0. No extension control for targeted file edits was found.

labels.text: AGI wants to start a browser task

S57.13.needs: a signed-in account allowed to run browser tasks, and a website to open
S57.13.note: Browser tasks use Chrome's debugger and ask for site access first.
steps: Send a message such as "Open example.com in the browser."
When the card "AGI wants to start a browser task" appears, click "Start task" (choose "Allow for this task" first if the site asks).
Watch the step "Opening …" in the answer's steps.
Check that a real browser tab opens to the site, and compare with Expected.
S57.13.where: Chat > ask it to open a website in the browser > on the card "AGI wants to start a browser task", click "Start task"

S57.14.needs: a signed-in account allowed to run browser tasks, and a website with a form or links
S57.14.note: Some actions can need your approval first, as the card explains.
steps: Send a task such as "Search this site for pricing and tell me the price." and click "Start task" on the card.
Watch the steps shown in the answer, such as "Clicking", "Typing" and "Scrolling".
Check that the page itself is clicked, typed in and scrolled.
Compare with Expected: each action should appear as a step with its result.
S57.14.where: Chat > start a browser task (as in S57.13) > watch the action steps on the page

S57.21.note: Saving and recalling during a turn is decided by the model; the Memory sheet is where the tester checks it.
steps: Click "More" in the side panel and click "Memory".
Type a fact into the box, click "Add", and check that it appears in the list.
In a chat, ask AGI to forget that fact and check that the notice asks you to choose "Forget" or "Keep".
Click "Forget" and reopen "Memory" to confirm the fact is gone.

S57.22.note: Calendar connectors have no MCP endpoint set, so the tool is off. No calendar control was found in apps/extension; the Connectors item only opens the web page.

S57.23.needs: a signed-in account with a messaging connector (for example Slack) connected
S57.23.note: If the menu shows a "coming soon" hint, connectors are not available for the account. The connector page is on the web app.
steps: Click the "Add attachment" (+) button and click "Connectors"; connect a messaging service on the web page that opens.
Back in the chat, ask AGI to read or send a message on that service.
When the approval card appears with "Approve" and "Decline", read it first.
Click "Approve" and compare: the message should be read or sent only after approval.
S57.23.where: Add attachment (+) > Connectors, then approve the request in the chat

S57.24.note: Not verified whether the Schedules section sits under Shortcuts on the settings page or in a separate section.
steps: In a chat, ask AGI to create a scheduled task, for example "Every weekday at 9am, summarise my notes."
Click "More" and click "Shortcuts" to open the settings page.
Find the "Schedules" section and check the new schedule appears with a "Next …" time.
Click "More" > "Tasks" to see runs, and compare with Expected.

S57.26.note: The model decides when to ask; the tester may need to ask for questions explicitly.
steps: Send a message that needs choices first, such as "Ask me questions before you plan a trip."
When the question card appears, pick an option for each question.
Click "Send answers" (or "I'll just type it" to answer in your own words).
Check that the answer continues using your choices, and compare with Expected.
S57.26.where: Chat > ask AGI to ask you questions before it answers > answer on the card and click "Send answers"

S57.28.note: The server tells the model which other tools exist and loads them on demand; no extension screen shows this.
S57.28.where: Not shown in the side panel; the effect is inside the model's turn

S57.29.note: Searched apps/extension for tool search and tool discovery labels. Only WebMCP page-tool discovery in src/content.ts was found, which is a different feature.

S57.30.note: The capabilities panel is on the web app (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx); its exact labels were not checked.
steps: Click the "Add attachment" (+) button and click "Connectors"; a web tab opens.
Open a connector in the list on that page.
Look at its tool list: each tool should show a readable description and its parameters.
Compare with Expected.
S57.30.where: Add attachment (+) > Connectors, then open a connector on the AGI web page and read its tools

S57.31.note: The arguments are shown as JSON in the step details.
steps: Send a question that makes AGI use a tool, such as a web search.
When the answer appears, click the "Worked for …" line under it.
Click a tool step to open its details.
Look for the "Request" heading and check the arguments shown (for example the search query).
S57.31.where: Chat > ask a question that uses a tool > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > click a tool step

steps: Send a question that makes AGI use a tool.
While it runs, look at the "Working for …" line and the step's spinning icon with its elapsed time.
When it ends, check the line changes to "Worked for …" and the step is marked done.
If a step fails, check the line says "Failed after …" and compare with Expected.
S57.32.where: Chat > ask a question that uses a tool > watch the "Working for …" line while it runs

S57.33.note: The one-line preview text is written by the server.
steps: Send a question that makes AGI use a tool.
When the answer appears, click the "Worked for …" line under it.
Read the short text on each finished tool step row.
Click that row and check the "Result" heading shows the result, as Expected says.
S57.33.where: Chat > ask a question that uses a tool > under the answer, click "Worked for …" and read the step line

steps: Send a question that makes AGI use a tool, then click the "Worked for …" line under the answer.
Click a finished tool step row to expand it and check the "Request" and "Result" headings.
Click the same row again to collapse it.
Compare the expanded and collapsed states with Expected.
S57.34.where: Chat > ask a question that uses a tool > under the answer, click "Worked for …" > click a tool step row

S57.36.needs: a chat where the assistant ran a tool with a long result
S57.36.note: Code found: the result is kept in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-result-store.ts and the reader is the model-facing tool read_tool_result (tool-result-store.ts:12). Its reference appears in the model's context notice, and the extension (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:1065) has no control or wording for reading a stored result. Its only visible name is 'Read a stored tool result' in apps/web/lib/tool-copy.ts, which is web-only. The extension shows the output it receives, but the trimming happens server-side, so the user cannot see the stored reference. Searched apps/extension for read_tool_result, tool-result, reference, and the stored-result wording: none found.

S57.37.needs: a chat where the assistant has run at least one tool
S57.37.note: The expandable step is built in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts (lines 1062-1065). I did not confirm that these steps are still shown after the chat is reopened or the side panel restarts, so 'later review' is unverified. The web-only 'Recent calls' log (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCallLog.tsx) is a separate record in the web app, not the extension.
steps: Sign in and open the side panel, then start a chat that makes the assistant use a tool, for example ask it to open a web page.
Wait until the tool step has finished and shows as completed.
Tap the tool step's row to expand it.
Look under the 'Request' heading for the input the tool received and under the 'Result' heading for what it returned, and compare with Expected: which tool ran, its input, and its outcome.
S57.37.where: Side panel chat > the assistant's tool step (its summary row) > tap the row to expand it > read the 'Request' and 'Result' headings
